subtopic: Law of Chemical Equilibrium and Equilibrium Constant
stem: The following concentrations were obtained for the formation of \(\text{NH}_3\) from \(\text{N}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\) at equilibrium at 500 K. \([\text{N}_2] = 1.5 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{M}\), \([\text{H}_2] = 3.0 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{M}\) and \([\text{NH}_3] = 1.2 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{M}\). Calculate equilibrium constant.
solution:
The equilibrium constant for the reaction, \(\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)\) can be written as,

\(K_c = \dfrac{[\text{NH}_3(g)]^2}{[\text{N}_2(g)][\text{H}_2(g)]^3}\)

\(= \dfrac{(1.2 \times 10^{-2})^2}{(1.5 \times 10^{-2})(3.0 \times 10^{-2})^3}\)

\(= 0.355 \times 10^3 = 3.55 \times 10^2\)

subtopic: Law of Chemical Equilibrium and Equilibrium Constant
stem:
At equilibrium, the concentrations of \(\text{N}_2 = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M}\), \(\text{O}_2 = 4.2 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M}\) and \(\text{NO} = 2.8 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M}\) in a sealed vessel at 800 K. What will be \(K_c\) for the reaction

\(\text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}(g)\)
solution:
For the reaction equilibrium constant, \(K_c\) can be written as,

\(K_c = \dfrac{[\text{NO}]^2}{[\text{N}_2][\text{O}_2]}\)

\(= \dfrac{(2.8 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M})^2}{(3.0 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M})(4.2 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{M})}\)

\(= 0.622\)

stem:
\(\text{PCl}_5\), \(\text{PCl}_3\) and \(\text{Cl}_2\) are at equilibrium at 500 K and having concentration \(1.59\,\text{M}\) \(\text{PCl}_3\), \(1.59\,\text{M}\) \(\text{Cl}_2\) and \(1.41\,\text{M}\) \(\text{PCl}_5\). Calculate \(K_c\) for the reaction,

\(\text{PCl}_5 \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2\)
solution:
The equilibrium constant \(K_c\) for the above reaction can be written as,

\(K_c = \dfrac{[\text{PCl}_3][\text{Cl}_2]}{[\text{PCl}_5]} = \dfrac{(1.59)^2}{(1.41)} = 1.79\)

stem:
The value of \(K_c = 4.24\) at 800 K for the reaction,

\(\text{CO}(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2(g)\)

Calculate equilibrium concentrations of \(\text{CO}_2\), \(\text{H}_2\), \(\text{CO}\) and \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) at 800 K, if only \(\text{CO}\) and \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) are present initially at concentrations of \(0.10\,\text{M}\) each.
solution:
For the reaction,

\(\text{CO}(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2(g)\)

Initial concentration: \(0.1\,\text{M}\), \(0.1\,\text{M}\), 0, 0.

Let \(x\) mole per litre of each of the product be formed.

At equilibrium: \((0.1-x)\,\text{M}\), \((0.1-x)\,\text{M}\), \(x\,\text{M}\), \(x\,\text{M}\), where \(x\) is the amount of \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\) at equilibrium.

Hence, equilibrium constant can be written as,

\(K_c = x^2/(0.1-x)^2 = 4.24\)

\(x^2 = 4.24(0.01 + x^2 - 0.2x)\)

\(x^2 = 0.0424 + 4.24x^2 - 0.848x\)

\(3.24x^2 - 0.848x + 0.0424 = 0\)

\(a = 3.24\), \(b = -0.848\), \(c = 0.0424\)

(for quadratic equation \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\))

\(x = [0.848 \pm \sqrt{(0.848)^2 - 4(3.24)(0.0424)}]/(3.24 \times 2)\)

\(x = (0.848 \pm 0.4118)/6.48\)

\(x_1 = (0.848 - 0.4118)/6.48 = 0.067\)

\(x_2 = (0.848 + 0.4118)/6.48 = 0.194\)

The value 0.194 should be neglected because it will give concentration of the reactant which is more than initial concentration.

Hence the equilibrium concentrations are,

\([\text{CO}_2] = [\text{H}_2] = x = 0.067\,\text{M}\)

\([\text{CO}] = [\text{H}_2\text{O}] = 0.1 - 0.067 = 0.033\,\text{M}\)

stem:
For the equilibrium,

\(2\text{NOCl}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)\)

the value of the equilibrium constant, \(K_c\) is \(3.75 \times 10^{-6}\) at 1069 K. Calculate the \(K_p\) for the reaction at this temperature?
solution:
We know that,

\(K_p = K_c(\text{R}T)^{\Delta n}\)

For the above reaction,

\(\Delta n = (2+1) - 2 = 1\)

\(K_p = 3.75 \times 10^{-6}(0.0831 \times 1069)\)

\(K_p = 0.033\)

stem:
The value of \(K_p\) for the reaction,

\(\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{C}(s) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}(g)\)

is 3.0 at 1000 K. If initially \(p_{\text{CO}_2} = 0.48\,\text{bar}\) and \(p_{\text{CO}} = 0\,\text{bar}\) and pure graphite is present, calculate the equilibrium partial pressures of \(\text{CO}\) and \(\text{CO}_2\).
solution:
For the reaction, let \(x\) be the decrease in pressure of \(\text{CO}_2\), then

\(\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{C}(s) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}(g)\)

Initial pressure: \(0.48\,\text{bar}\), \(0\)

At equilibrium: \((0.48 - x)\,\text{bar}\), \(2x\,\text{bar}\)

\(K_p = \dfrac{p_{\text{CO}}^2}{p_{\text{CO}_2}}\)

\(K_p = (2x)^2/(0.48 - x) = 3\)

\(4x^2 = 3(0.48 - x)\)

\(4x^2 = 1.44 - x\)

\(4x^2 + 3x - 1.44 = 0\)

\(a = 4\), \(b = 3\), \(c = -1.44\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\)

\(= [-3 \pm \sqrt{(3)^2 - 4(4)(-1.44)}]/(2 \times 4)\)

\(= (-3 \pm 5.66)/8\)

\(= (-3 + 5.66)/8\) (as value of \(x\) cannot be negative hence we neglect that value)

\(x = 2.66/8 = 0.33\)

The equilibrium partial pressures are,

\(p_{\text{CO}} = 2x = 2 \times 0.33 = 0.66\,\text{bar}\)

\(p_{\text{CO}_2} = 0.48 - x = 0.48 - 0.33 = 0.15\,\text{bar}\)
_note: Book defect preserved in intent: the printed solution labels BOTH final partial pressures as p_CO2 — the first (2x = 0.66 bar) is the pressure of CO, as its own working (K_p = p_CO^2/p_CO2) requires. The label has been set to p_CO here because printing it as p_CO2 would make the solution self-contradictory.

stem: The value of \(K_c\) for the reaction \(2\text{A} \rightleftharpoons \text{B} + \text{C}\) is \(2 \times 10^{-3}\). At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is \([\text{A}] = [\text{B}] = [\text{C}] = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{M}\). In which direction the reaction will proceed?
solution:
For the reaction the reaction quotient \(Q_c\) is given by,

\(Q_c = [\text{B}][\text{C}]/[\text{A}]^2\)

as \([\text{A}] = [\text{B}] = [\text{C}] = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{M}\)

\(Q_c = (3 \times 10^{-4})(3 \times 10^{-4})/(3 \times 10^{-4})^2 = 1\)

as \(Q_c > K_c\) so the reaction will proceed in the reverse direction.

stem:
\(13.8\,\text{g}\) of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4\) was placed in a \(1\,\text{L}\) reaction vessel at 400 K and allowed to attain equilibrium

\(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g)\)

The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be \(9.15\,\text{bar}\). Calculate \(K_c\), \(K_p\) and partial pressure at equilibrium.
solution:
We know \(pV = n\text{R}T\)

Total volume \((V) = 1\,\text{L}\)

Molecular mass of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4 = 92\,\text{g}\)

Number of moles \(= 13.8\,\text{g}/92\,\text{g} = 0.15\) of the gas \((n)\)

Gas constant \((\text{R}) = 0.083\,\text{bar L mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)

Temperature \((T) = 400\,\text{K}\)

\(p \times 1\,\text{L} = 0.15\,\text{mol} \times 0.083\,\text{bar L mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \times 400\,\text{K}\)

\(p = 4.98\,\text{bar}\)

\(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2\)

Initial pressure: \(4.98\,\text{bar}\), \(0\)

At equilibrium: \((4.98 - x)\,\text{bar}\), \(2x\,\text{bar}\)

Hence, \(p_{\text{total}}\) at equilibrium \(= p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_4} + p_{\text{NO}_2}\)

\(9.15 = (4.98 - x) + 2x\)

\(9.15 = 4.98 + x\)

\(x = 9.15 - 4.98 = 4.17\,\text{bar}\)

Partial pressures at equilibrium are,

\(p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_4} = 4.98 - 4.17 = 0.81\,\text{bar}\)

\(p_{\text{NO}_2} = 2x = 2 \times 4.17 = 8.34\,\text{bar}\)

\(K_p = (p_{\text{NO}_2})^2/p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_4} = (8.34)^2/0.81 = 85.87\)

\(K_p = K_c(\text{R}T)^{\Delta n}\)

\(85.87 = K_c(0.083 \times 400)^1\)

\(K_c = 2.586 = 2.6\)

stem: \(3.00\,\text{mol}\) of \(\text{PCl}_5\) kept in \(1\,\text{L}\) closed reaction vessel was allowed to attain equilibrium at 380 K. Calculate composition of the mixture at equilibrium. \(K_c = 1.80\)

subtopic: Relationship Between Equilibrium Constant K, Reaction Quotient Q and Gibbs Energy G
stem: The value of \(\Delta G^\ominus\) for the phosphorylation of glucose in glycolysis is \(13.8\,\text{kJ/mol}\). Find the value of \(K_c\) at 298 K.
solution:
\(\Delta G^\ominus = 13.8\,\text{kJ/mol} = 13.8 \times 10^3\,\text{J/mol}\)

Also, \(\Delta G^\ominus = -\text{R}T \ln K_c\)

Hence, \(\ln K_c = \dfrac{-13.8 \times 10^3\,\text{J/mol}}{8.314\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \times 298\,\text{K}}\)

\(\ln K_c = -5.569\)

\(K_c = e^{-5.569}\)

\(K_c = 3.81 \times 10^{-3}\)

subtopic: Relationship Between Equilibrium Constant K, Reaction Quotient Q and Gibbs Energy G
stem:
Hydrolysis of sucrose gives,

Sucrose \(+\ \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons\) Glucose \(+\) Fructose

Equilibrium constant \(K_c\) for the reaction is \(2 \times 10^{13}\) at 300 K. Calculate \(\Delta G^\ominus\) at 300 K.
solution:
\(\Delta G^\ominus = -\text{R}T \ln K_c\)

\(\Delta G^\ominus = -8.314\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \times 300\,\text{K} \times \ln(2 \times 10^{13})\)

\(\Delta G^\ominus = -7.64 \times 10^4\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\)
